cards.intuition: Hash the key into a bucket, then resolve collisions among keys sharing that bucket. Good distribution keeps the candidate group small.
cards.topic: Hash Tables: Buckets, Collisions, and Load Factor

cards.intuition: Load factor measures how crowded the bucket array is. Crowding lengthens chains or probe sequences and eventually forces resizing.
cards.formula: alpha = entries / buckets; chained expected lookup O(1 + alpha)
cards.topic: Hash Tables: Buckets, Collisions, and Load Factor

cards.intuition: A resize is expensive but rare when capacity grows geometrically. Spread each occasional rebuild across the many cheap inserts it enables.
cards.formula: geometric resizing gives amortized O(1) insertion
cards.topic: Hash Tables: Buckets, Collisions, and Load Factor

cards.intuition: A tail pointer lets the list attach a new final node without moving existing postings. The bargain is cheap growth in exchange for pointer-heavy traversal.
cards.topic: Linked Lists as Postings: Sequential Access and Cheap Append

cards.intuition: Scattered nodes waste cache-line payload and reveal each next address only after the current node arrives. Binary search cannot jump to a midpoint.
cards.formula: positional access and worst-case search = O(n)
cards.topic: Linked Lists as Postings: Sequential Access and Cheap Append

cards.intuition: Accept writes in a flexible in-memory structure, then flatten them into compact sorted bytes for serving. Separate structures let ingestion and queries each get the layout they need.
cards.formula: buffer updates → sort and flush → immutable contiguous segment
cards.topic: Linked Lists as Postings: Sequential Access and Cheap Append

cards.intuition: Contiguous IDs support direct addressing, binary search, sequential intersection, prefetching, and block compression. One cache line carries many useful values.
cards.topic: Arrays vs Linked Lists for Postings Storage

cards.intuition: Write into spare capacity until full, then copy into a geometrically larger block. A resize spikes one operation but average append remains constant.
cards.formula: amortized append O(1); resizing append O(n)
cards.topic: Arrays vs Linked Lists for Postings Storage

cards.intuition: Pointer splicing is constant time only when the predecessor is already known. Searching for the insertion position can still scan the full list.
cards.topic: Arrays vs Linked Lists for Postings Storage

cards.intuition: Hashing optimizes exact identity; sorting preserves neighborhood. Prefixes, ranges, lower bounds, and ordered merges need neighborhood information.
cards.formula: hash exact lookup expected O(1); sorted exact lookup O(log n)
cards.topic: Hash Map vs Sorted Structure: When Order Matters

cards.intuition: Binary-search the first possible key, then stream consecutive matches until the range ends. Work scales with search depth plus actual output.
cards.formula: range query = O(log n + k) for k outputs
cards.topic: Hash Map vs Sorted Structure: When Order Matters

cards.concept: Order is part of the data contract
cards.intuition: Choose structures from required operations, not one benchmark. If clients need nearest keys, ranges, prefixes, or merges, unordered constant-time lookup is incomplete.
cards.formula: get only: hash; ordered operations: sorted structure
cards.topic: Hash Map vs Sorted Structure: When Order Matters
